knowledge_checks.title: Active Recall: 2.6.1
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. Which statement correctly defines a random sample from a population?
knowledge_checks.body: Select the sampling warrant for inference.
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: Random-sample status comes from the selection mechanism and population relationship, not from sample size or observed summaries.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: Observations must follow the stated sampling model, usually iid draws from the target population.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Treating an available data extract as random without examining how it was selected.

choices.label: A random sample consists of observations generated from the stated population under a sampling model, commonly iid draws. A collection of n observations is not automatically representative or independent.
Any n observations form a random sample once their sample mean and variance can be calculated.
A sample is random exactly when its sample mean equals the population mean.
Sampling design is irrelevant after an estimator formula has been selected.

knowledge_checks.title: Checkpoint: 2.6.1
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. An analyst takes the 40 most recent claims from one client as a sample of the whole motor book. Which statement is correct?
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: Selection from one client does not represent an iid draw from the whole motor portfolio.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: Not random for the whole book; selection and dependence remain despite n=40.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Using sample size or a matching mean as evidence that the selection mechanism was random.

choices.label: The extract is not a random sample of the whole book: one client's consecutive claims create selection and possible dependence. Having 40 observations does not repair that sampling mechanism.
It is random because n=40 exceeds a common large-sample threshold.
It becomes random if its mean happens to be close to the whole-book mean.
Choosing a t statistic later will correct any client-level selection bias.

worked_example.title: Classify a severity-truncated slice as not a random sample
worked_example.problem_statement: An analyst keeps only the first 25 claims whose settled cost exceeds £10,000 from a national household book and treats that list as a random sample from all household claims in order to estimate portfolio mean severity. Decide whether this extract is a random sample from the stated population, and name the sampling defect.

given.value: all household claims in the national book

worked_example.attempt_before_reveal: CMP closed. Compare the severity-truncation mechanism with an iid (or otherwise stated) draw from all household claims before judging the sample label.

steps.label: State what a random sample requires
steps.attempt_cue: Name the warrant that links observations to the population distribution.
steps.explanation: A random sample is drawn so that observations follow the population distribution under a stated sampling model (for example iid draws). Estimators and intervals inherit that warrant.
steps.calculation: Require: stated sampling model linking extract to all-household-claim population
steps.result: Random sample = lawful draw under a sampling model

steps.label: Inspect the actual selection mechanism
steps.attempt_cue: Describe how the 25 claims were chosen.
steps.explanation: Keeping only claims above £10,000 truncates the severity distribution and over-represents large losses relative to the full household book. Order of arrival does not repair that truncation.
steps.calculation: Mechanism = severity truncation above £10,000 (selection on the outcome)
steps.result: Selection is truncated / outcome-dependent, not portfolio random

steps.label: Classify and refuse n-as-warrant
steps.attempt_cue: Decide yes/no on random sample, and say why n = 25 alone fails.
steps.explanation: Having twenty-five observations does not create a random sample. Without a lawful draw from all household claims, estimator procedures lack the sampling warrant.
steps.calculation: Classification: NOT a random sample from all household claims; defect = severity truncation / selection on Y
steps.result: Not a random sample; n alone is insufficient

worked_example.final_answer: Not a random sample from all household claims: keeping only costs above £10,000 truncates severity. n = 25 does not by itself create a random sample.
worked_example.common_pitfall: Treating any large enough extract as a random sample because n = 25 looks adequate, without checking whether the draw matches the stated all-claims population.
